overview: I do not recognise the Ross Gambit by name. The root is 1.Nf3 e5, which White can meet by 2.Nxe5 winning a pawn, so the gambit is probably Black's: Black replies ...Nc6 and ...Qe7 or similar for development after 2.Nxe5. More commonly White plays 2.Nc3 or 2.e4 and it transposes to a Four Knights or Petrov-like game.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with 2.Nxe5 and trade the active piece.
Or transpose with 2.Nc3 or 2.e4 into a normal open game.

black_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with ...Nc6 and use open lines for the pawn.
Hold the e5 pawn and play the reversed Open Game.

typical_structures.structure: Open game structure with e-pawns exchanged or Black pawn missing.

character.notes: Unclear; quiet if White transposes, tactical if White takes on e5.

gambit.notes: My assumption: after 2.Nxe5 Black plays on a pawn down.

soundness.notes: Probably dubious for Black if it is a gambit, but not sure.

character.reason: Unsure; the main line is probably quiet.

gambit.reason: Assumed from the gambit name and 2.Nxe5.

soundness.reason: A pawn down for little if it is a gambit.
